translation_en: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Zakariyya narrated to us, from Amir, from Urwah al-Bariqi, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection: reward and spoils.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl and Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Husayn, from al-Shabi, from Urwah al-Bariqi, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Good is tied to the forelocks of horses. He was asked: Messenger of Allah, what is that good? He said: Reward and spoils until the Day of Resurrection.
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Jarir informed us, from Husayn, with this chain, except that he said: Urwah ibn al-Jad.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Khalaf ibn Hisham, and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah all report from Abu al-Ahwas. [Another chain:] Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Abi Umar both report from Sufyan. All report from Shabib ibn Gharqadah, from Urwah al-Bariqi, from the Prophet. They did not mention reward and spoils. In Sufyan's report, it says that Urwah al-Bariqi heard the Prophet.

Ubaydullah ibn Muadh narrated to us: My father narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar said: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us. Both report from Shubah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Ayzar ibn Hurayth, from Urwah ibn al-Jad, from the Prophet, with this report, but they did not mention 'reward and spoils.'

Ubaydullah ibn Muadh narrated to us: My father narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar said: Yahya ibn Said narrated to us. Both report from Shubah, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Blessing is in the forelocks of horses.

Yahya ibn Habib narrated to us: Khalid (Ibn al-Harith) narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us. Both said: Shubah narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who heard Anas narrate from the Prophet, with a similar report.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us. Yahya said: He informed us; the others said: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salm ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Zurah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah disliked a horse with a white marking on diagonally opposite legs.

Muhammad ibn Numayr narrated this to us: My father narrated to us. [Another chain:] Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated to me: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us. Both report from Sufyan with this chain and a similar report. Abd al-Razzaq's hadith adds: A shikal is when a horse has white on its right hind leg and left foreleg, or on its right foreleg and left hind leg.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad (Ibn Jafar) narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us. Both report from Shubah, from Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Nakhai, from Abu Zurah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, with a report like Waki's hadith. In Wahb's narration it is from Abdullah ibn Yazid, and he did not mention al-Nakhai.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Umarah (Ibn al-Qaqa), from Abu Zurah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Allah guarantees Paradise for the one who sets out in His cause, and nothing makes him leave except striving in My cause, belief in Me, and affirming My messengers. He is guaranteed that I will admit him to Paradise or return him to the home from which he departed, with whatever reward or spoils he gained. By the One in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, any wound inflicted in Allah's cause will come on the Day of Resurrection as it was when inflicted: its color will be the color of blood and its smell will be musk. By the One in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, were it not that it would burden the Muslims, I would never stay behind a detachment going out to fight in Allah's cause. But I have no means to provide mounts for them, and they have no means themselves, and it is hard for them to remain behind me. By the One in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, I wish I could fight in Allah's cause, be killed, fight again, be killed, then fight again and be killed.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Umarah, with this chain.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: al-Mughirah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hizami informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: Allah guarantees for the one who strives in His cause, and nothing makes him leave his home except striving in Allah's cause and affirming His word, that He will admit him to Paradise or return him to the home from which he departed with whatever reward or spoils he gained.

Amr al-Naqid and Zuhayr ibn Harb said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: No one is wounded in Allah's cause—and Allah knows best who is wounded in His cause—except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound flowing: its color will be the color of blood and its smell the smell of musk.

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Mamar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah. He mentioned several hadiths, including that the Messenger of Allah said: Every wound a Muslim receives in Allah's cause will appear on the Day of Resurrection as it was when he was pierced, flowing with blood; its color will be the color of blood, and its scent the scent of musk. The Messenger of Allah also said: By the One in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, were it not that I would burden the believers, I would never stay behind a detachment going out to fight in Allah's cause. But I have no means to provide mounts for them, and they have no means to follow me, and they are not content to stay behind me.

Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: Were it not that I would burden the believers, I would not stay behind a detachment. He reported a hadith like theirs. With this same chain, he also reported: By the One in whose hand is my soul, I wish I could be killed in Allah's cause and then brought back to life, with a report like Abu Zurah's hadith from Abu Hurayrah.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab (al-Thaqafi) narrated to us. [Another chain:] Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Marwan ibn Muawiyah narrated to us. All report from Yahya ibn Said, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Were it not that I would burden my community, I would love never to stay behind a detachment. It is like their hadith.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Allah guarantees for the one who sets out in His cause—up to where he said—'I would not stay behind a detachment going out to fight in Allah Most High's cause.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Shubah, from Qatadah and Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, who said: No soul that has a good standing with Allah would wish to return to the world, even if it were given the world and all it contains, except the martyr. He wishes to return and be killed in this world because of the virtue of martyrdom that he sees.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar said: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrate from the Prophet, who said: No one who enters Paradise would wish to return to the world and have everything on earth, except the martyr. He wishes to return and be killed ten times because of the honor he sees.

Said ibn Mansur narrated to us: Khalid ibn Abdullah al-Wasiti narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet was asked: What can equal striving in the cause of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? He said: You cannot do it. They asked him again two or three times, and each time he said: You cannot do it. On the third occasion he said: The example of one who strives in Allah's cause is like that of one who fasts, stands in prayer, and recites Allah's verses without tiring of fasting or prayer until the one striving in Allah's cause returns.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us. [Another chain:] Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us. [Another chain:] Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us. All report from Suhayl with this chain and a similar report.

Hasan ibn Ali al-Hulwani narrated to me: Abu Tawbah narrated to us: Muawiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Sallam, who heard Abu Sallam say: al-Numan ibn Bashir narrated to me: I was at the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah when a man said: I would not mind doing no deed after Islam except giving pilgrims water to drink. Another man said: I would not mind doing no deed after Islam except maintaining the Sacred Mosque. Another man said: Striving in the cause of Allah is better than what you have said. Umar rebuked them and said: Do not raise your voices near the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah; it is Friday. When I have prayed Friday prayer, I will go in and ask him for a ruling about what you disagree over. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: 'Do you consider giving water to pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in Allah and the Last Day...' (Quran 9:19), through the end of the verse.

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated this to me: Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us: Muawiyah narrated to us: Zayd informed me that he heard Abu Sallam say: al-Numan ibn Bashir narrated to me: I was at the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah, with a report like Abu Tawbah's hadith.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qanab narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: A morning or evening journey in Allah's cause is better than the world and all it contains.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim informed us, from his father, from Sahl ibn Sad al-Saidi, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: A morning journey a servant makes in Allah's cause is better than the world and all it contains.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb said: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sad al-Saidi, from the Prophet, who said: A morning or evening journey in Allah's cause is better than the world and all it contains.

Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Marwan ibn Muawiyah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Said, from Dhakwan ibn Abi Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Were it not that men from my community... He related the hadith and said in it: An evening or morning journey in Allah's cause is better than the world and all it contains.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us; the wording is Abu Bakr's and Ishaq's. Ishaq said: He informed us; the other two said: Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us, from Said ibn Abi Ayyub: Shurahbil ibn Sharik al-Maafiri narrated to me, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, who said: I heard Abu Ayyub say: The Messenger of Allah said: A morning or evening journey in Allah's cause is better than everything upon which the sun rises and sets.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Qahzadh narrated to me: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, who said: Said ibn Abi Ayyub and Haywah ibn Shurayh informed us, each of them saying: Shurahbil ibn Sharik narrated to me, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, who heard Abu Ayyub al-Ansari say: The Messenger of Allah said the same.
